purpose: Enumerate every architecture-specific execution path so that each one can be held to bit-identical output against a portable reference. Registering a path here is the precondition for the cross-ISA bit-identity gate; an unregistered ISA path must fail the gate closed.

method.static_scan: ripgrep over crates/*/src for core::arch::*, is_*_feature_detected, target_arch/target_feature cfg, std::simd and core::simd
method.limits: Static inventory. Cross-machine execution on AArch64 and Windows x64 was NOT performed in this session (no such hardware available); those lanes remain open on the bead.

totals._note: target_arch_cfg_sites was 57 when this inventory was first written on 2026-07-24 and is 62 today. The gate caught that drift on its first run, which is the behaviour it exists for: a new architecture-specific site is a deliberate engineering act and the inventory must acknowledge it. The 2026-07-24 pass also split core::arch counts by target architecture; the gate measures core::arch:: as one metric because splitting it needs a parse rather than a scan, and an unmeasurable declared total is worse than an honest combined one. 2026-07-26: no counts changed, but the swar-lexer entry's compliance verdict was corrected -- its cited equivalence mechanism tested only the 8-lane aggregate and was near-vacuous, and a real per-lane SWAR/scalar disagreement was found and fixed underneath it.

key_structural_finding.statement: There are currently ZERO real ISA-specific EXECUTION paths in the runtime. The module named simd_lexer.rs does not use SIMD intrinsics at all: its own header states it uses SWAR (SIMD Within A Register) via ordinary 64-bit arithmetic with no unsafe code and no platform intrinsics. The handful of is_*_feature_detected calls are confined to building an architecture FINGERPRINT for telemetry and reproducibility reporting, not to dispatching divergent code.
key_structural_finding.consequence: Current cross-ISA divergence risk is LOW, and the same machine code runs everywhere. The risk becomes real and large the moment BRIDGE-10.2 (AArch64/NEON code shapes) and BRIDGE-11.2 (Zen4/Zen5 AVX-512 kernels) land, and again for BRIDGE-07.20 guarded vectorization.
key_structural_finding.revises: This tempers the original framing of this bead. The gate should be understood as a PRECONDITION to be installed before ISA paths are introduced, not as remediation of existing divergence. Installing it now is cheap; installing it after twenty vectorized kernels exist is not.

registered_paths.kind: SWAR (portable 64-bit word arithmetic) - NOT an ISA-specific path
registered_paths.portable_counterpart: scalar reference lexer in the same module
registered_paths.equivalence_mechanism: Two layers. (a) LEXER LEVEL: find_mismatch(swar, scalar) -> Option<ParityMismatch>, the surviving control from the bd-2noh9 fix, plus the DifferentialLexer parity tests. (b) MASK LEVEL (added 2026-07-26): swar_masks_match_scalar_reference_in_every_lane_exhaustively compares each SWAR mask against a byte-loop reference LANE BY LANE over every byte value in every lane against boundary-adjacent fills; plus swar_masks_match_scalar_reference_on_adversarial_words, swar_range_masks_are_lane_local_under_borrow_pressure, and three length/alignment differentials (swar_scalar_parity_across_every_length_through_five_words sweeps len 0..=40 at every phase, swar_scalar_parity_on_unaligned_starts, swar_scalar_parity_on_word_boundary_straddling_tokens). Fuzz: crates/franken-engine/fuzz/fuzz_targets/swar_scalar_boundary_differential.rs.
registered_paths.precedent: bd-2noh9 was a real shipped SWAR-vs-scalar lexical-token divergence. The parity mechanism above is the surviving control from that fix and MUST NOT be removed.
registered_paths.verdict: COMPLIANT at both lexer and mask level as of 2026-07-26. Was NOT compliant at mask level before that date, despite this entry asserting it was; see equivalence_mechanism_correction_20260726.
registered_paths.residual_risk: LOW. SWAR is ordinary integer arithmetic and therefore deterministic across ISAs; endianness is the only theoretical concern and all supported targets are little-endian. The lane-locality hazard that produced the 2026-07-26 defect is now covered by exhaustive per-lane tests, so a reformulation that reintroduces cross-lane borrow fails closed.

equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.what_this_entry_used_to_claim: 'COMPLIANT - portable counterpart exists and is differentially tested', citing swar_all_word_predicates_match_scalar_reference as the mechanism.
equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.why_that_was_wrong: That test compares only the all-eight-lanes AGGREGATE of each predicate, and for pseudo-random words the aggregate is almost never true: P(all 8 bytes ASCII whitespace) is about (6/256)^8 ~ 1.4e-13, P(all 8 digits) ~ 5.5e-13. Across its 20,000 iterations the interesting branch is essentially never taken, so it is overwhelmingly assert_eq!(false, false). It could not observe a per-lane defect, and it did not.
equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.defect_found: digit_mask and alpha_mask used a wrapping_sub range compare. Subtraction borrows propagate low->high across lane boundaries, so a lane's result depended on its neighbours: the SWAR masks disagreed with their own scalar reference.
equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.severity_established_by_proof_not_assert: Exhaustive case analysis over the lane transfer function (all 256 byte values x both borrow-in states = complete enumeration, not a sample) found 4 disagreeing cases for the digit range and 8 for alpha. EVERY one was a false NEGATIVE, and none occurred with no incoming borrow, i.e. never in lane 0. Since match_prefix_len counts LEADING lanes and stops at the first clear one, a false negative only shortened the SWAR advance and the scalar tail loop finished the token correctly. Observable lexer output was therefore never wrong; the cost was throughput, not correctness.
equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.why_it_was_fixed_rather_than_documented: That safety argument is a property of the two current CALL SITES, not of the mask functions. mask_first_set, mask_popcount, or any future vectorized builtin consuming these masks would inherit a silent wrong answer. Under this bead's own scope item 1 a SWAR path must be bit-identical to its portable reference on its own terms.
equivalence_mechanism_correction_2026072.fix: Carry-free formulation: mask to 7 bits per lane, add (0x80 - bound) so a lane's high bit sets exactly when it reaches the bound and cannot carry into the next lane (0x7F + (0x80 - bound) <= 0xFF), and exclude high-bit bytes explicitly. Verified exhaustively: 196,608 lane comparisons, zero mismatches.

gate_contract.rule: For every architecture-specific code path, the ISA-specialised implementation and the portable reference implementation MUST produce bit-identical observable output on the same input.
gate_contract.enforcement: The gate fails closed on (a) any observed divergence, and (b) any new architecture-specific path that lacks a registered portable counterpart in this inventory.
gate_contract.boundary_fuzzing_required: Inputs at and around vector-width boundaries, unaligned starts, and tail handling - this is precisely where the bd-2noh9 defect class lives.
gate_contract.feature_detection_rule: Runtime detection only, never compile-time-only, so a binary built on one machine stays correct on another.
gate_contract.determinism_outranks_speed: Any ISA path that cannot be proven bit-identical is disabled by default and may ship only behind a non-default flag with a recorded waiver.

fingerprint_containment_finding.statement: Verified 2026-07-26: ArchCapabilityProfile, ArchFamily, SwarDisableReason and the *_available capability flags appear in NO src/ file other than simd_lexer.rs, and compute_token_witness_hash mixes only a domain tag, the input hash, the token count and per-token (kind, start, end). No architecture fact reaches a content hash today.
fingerprint_containment_finding.why_it_matters: FE-CLAIM-023 claims cross-platform identical-hash reproducibility. A detected CPU feature reaching a content hash would falsify it -- not through a defect in the hash, but by feeding it a host fact. Host facts belong in env.json.
fingerprint_containment_finding.enforcement: scripts/check_isa_path_registration.py checks 2 and 3. Containment is what makes check 3 complete rather than a spot check: a type confined to one module cannot reach a hash in another.
fingerprint_containment_finding.note_on_actual_mode: LexerTokenWitnessLog.actual_mode is host-dependent -- it records the mode the fallback matrix selected, which consults ArchCapabilityProfile::detect(). It is currently outside every content hash and the witness log is not referenced anywhere else in src/. If that log is ever folded into a hashed artifact, actual_mode must be excluded or the claim breaks.
